one_star_reviews.text: Avoid Mr Lattimer and any of his companies. Poor service

My business had high expectations after a very positive initial meeting, but unfortunately the service that followed was deeply disappointing.

After being handed over to operations, communication was extremely poor from the outset. I had to chase to find out when work was starting, I never had a clear sense of what was being done or why, and when I raised concerns, it became clear that assumptions had been made instead of there being any kind of proper strategy discussion. Reporting was also weak, with little explanation provided, and at one point I was even sent an SEO report for another business.

What stood out most was the complete lack of care and attention. I did not feel valued as a client, and I did not feel there was any proper care taken in how my account was managed.

When I later raised these concerns, the response was effectively that I was on the Bronze package. In my view, regardless of package level, if a client is paying for a service, there should still be a proper standard of care, attention, communication and professionalism at all times throughout the contract lifecycle.

My final issue is that, despite the investment made over the contract period, I have finished this engagement with no clear understanding of what impact the work actually had or what value it delivered, if any at all. That should never be the case with a professional SEO service.

To their credit, they did acknowledge some of the communication and process issues when I complained. However, I was disappointed with how the matter was ultimately handled. Sometimes when a service falls short, the way a company responds can help restore confidence, but I did not feel that happened here.

This review is simply an honest reflection of my experience. Based on that experience, I would not use this company again or recommend them to others.

Awareness review - I had a very disappointing experience with the Furniture Village Watford branch a few months ago. I wish I could give zero stars
We purchased a bed, mattress, and rug in-store for our new home. While we were happy with the bed and mattress, the issue began with the rug. What was delivered looked completely different from what we had seen and ordered in-store.

As anyone who has recently bought a house knows, budgeting is tight and every purchase is carefully planned. This rug was not a small purchase, so receiving something that didn’t match expectations was extremely frustrating.

When I contacted customer care, they initially refused to accept a return. I had to repeatedly explain and push for a resolution, as the rug was clearly not suitable and did not match what was displayed. I was then directed to the store, where I was initially told nothing could be done. Only after escalating to the store manager, Adnan, was I asked to send photos for comparison with the in-store sample.

After several days of follow-ups, I was told the supplier claimed the rug was “supposed to be darker” and would “fade over time”which is not an acceptable justification when the product looks significantly different at the time of delivery.

Despite continuing to request a fair resolution, I was asked to come into the store. When we did, my husband was made to carry the large rug without any assistance. We were treated dismissively, made to wait for hours, and made to feel like we were at fault. Eventually, we were told the rug could be returned but only with a 25% deduction. We felt pressured into accepting this as no reasonable alternative was offered.

To make matters worse, the refund was not provided as cash or to the original payment method but instead forced us into a store credit, limiting us to purchase again from Furniture Village.

We then selected a smaller rug and a lamp. However, even this was mishandled—our order was never processed. After waiting four weeks (when delivery was promised within two), I called to follow up and was told there was no record of any order. Thankfully, I had taken a photo of the receipt (despite resistance from the store manager  when I tried to do so), which I had to provide as proof before the order was finally processed.

Overall, this experience was stressful, time-consuming, and deeply disappointing. The lack of accountability, poor customer service, and dismissive attitude—particularly from the store manager made the situation far worse.

My takeaway: if you are considering purchasing from Furniture Village, avoid buying in-store. Ordering online may offer better consumer protection and a smoother returns process.

one_star_reviews.text:
After seven years of owning a No Letting Go franchise, I can honestly say the experience has caused me more stress, anxiety, financial pressure, and emotional exhaustion than I ever believed possible from a business relationship.

Throughout my ownership, I was repeatedly charged fees and amounts that were never properly outlined or agreed within the original contract terms. One of the most concerning examples was being charged £1,250 + VAT for “training” that was never actually provided.

At one stage, I was threatened with losing my franchise entirely because No Letting Go claimed I owed them nearly £6,000. The stress and worry this caused myself and my family was immense. However, once a full reconciliation of the accounts was eventually completed, it transpired that No Letting Go actually owed me approximately £2,000. Despite the seriousness of the accusations made against me, no formal apology was ever issued.

Franchisees are also charged a £200 + VAT monthly marketing fee, yet during my entire ownership I never once received a proper transparent breakdown showing exactly where this money was being spent.

The reality of the franchise is, in my opinion, very different from what is presented when purchasing. The deductions and ongoing fees are far higher than initially explained. Head office take a percentage of all national work alongside additional levies and charges that are not properly highlighted at the outset.

One of the most serious issues throughout my time with the company was the handling of confidential financial information. On numerous occasions, my financial data was breached and shared with third parties by the finance department. These breaches were never formally acknowledged, properly investigated, or rectified, and issues surrounding the mishandling of confidential information continued right up until very recently.

The introduction of the new software system was catastrophic across the network. Franchisees were forced onto a system that simply did not function properly. Offices lost clients, businesses lost income, people lost jobs, and franchise owners were left trying to deal with angry clients whilst also trying to protect their own livelihoods. The software remained unfit for purpose for close to two years, yet franchisees were still expected to absorb the financial and emotional consequences with little support or consideration for the stress being caused to owners and their families.

Franchisees are also charged for annual conferences even if they are unable to attend for entirely valid reasons.

Communication from the company has consistently been poor. Financial statements are confusing, overly complicated, and frequently appear inaccurate or out of date, creating constant disputes and unnecessary stress.

I officially sold my business effective from 1st April. The purchaser has now been operating and running the business for approximately six weeks, and from a contractual perspective the transfer has already taken place. Despite this, the sale funds continue to be withheld whilst excuses and delays continue.

The stress this ongoing situation has caused has been overwhelming. Instead of being allowed to move on after seven difficult years, I am now being forced into a position where I have had to seek legal advice, instruct a solicitor, and approach the British Franchise Association for assistance in trying to recover money that is rightfully owed to me. It genuinely feels as though games are being played whilst my finances and wellbeing continue to suffer.

I would never normally write a review like this, but after seven years of ongoing issues, stress, financial disputes, lack of transparency, and the way matters continue to be handled even after the sale of my business, I feel people deserve to know the reality of my experience.

Based on my personal experience, I would strongly advise anyone considering purchasing a franchise with No Letting Go to proceed with extreme caution.

We initially contacted Signature because of the funding they were advertising. The representative himself was pleasant enough, but there was a strong emphasis on how much better they are than other companies. He even showed us quotes from other companies (for jobs they supposedly completed for cheaper) with very high prices, seemingly to make their own quote appear more competitive.
They offered just over £3,600 in funding, bringing the total down to a bit over £8,500. However, it felt as though the original pre-funding price was inflated simply to make the “discounted” price look more appealing and that the reduced figure was likely closer to their real price.

Our advice would be to thoroughly research (bespoke windows aren't needed for a good fit or look) and speak to smaller, family-run businesses before committing to a larger company and a significant quote.

Having recently moved to the Greater Manchester area, I found this clinic through Google. Unfortunately, this was one of the worst aesthetics experiences I have had, and I genuinely wish I had researched more thoroughly before booking.

The injection/needling technique was unbelievably aggressive. I have previously been treated by doctors in London and immediately recognised the difference in skill, precision, and overall technique. This treatment felt unnecessarily forceful, traumatic, and lacking in finesse. There was very little care taken to ensure the procedure felt controlled, refined, or comfortable, and the lack of proper massage/shaping afterwards only made the overall result and experience feel worse.

What shocked me further was later seeing videos on social media of the doctor performing treatments in the exact same rough manner I experienced first hand. I also noticed multiple comments from other people pointing out how aggressive the technique appeared, which completely validated my concerns.

I honestly do not understand the overwhelming 5 star reviews surrounding this clinic. In my personal opinion, the aesthetic standard here leans heavily toward an overdone look rather than genuinely clean and natural results. If you are someone who values subtle, elegant and refined aesthetics and careful technique, I would strongly advise doing extensive research before committing to treatment here. The regular clientele here must clearly have a different taste and the clinic maybe attracts a different crowd? I have also heard from professionals that the doctor here likes the overdone look and what they see as ‘natural’ may actually come across as 'overdone' to the opposite crowd. But these are just opinions!

I just found my experience very odd and the doctors communication style felt off. I have also seen a few comments online (I will not disclose where) which gave me re assurance that I'm not the only one who feels this way.

The only positive part of my experience was the gentleman on reception, who was so warm and friendly and convenient parking.

one_star_reviews.text: MCS cancelled 2 appointments with us for a boiler service. We paid upfront. Waisted a days holiday from work as 1st appointment was cancelled at short notice.

I contacted this company to repair my Samsung air source heat pump. Initially, they attended within two days, and I paid a £120 call-out fee based on their confidence that they could fix the issue.

The engineer diagnosed a faulty fan motor and blade and said I’d have a quote and the work completed “early the following week”.

From that point on, the experience went downhill.

I had to chase them repeatedly over the following week just to get a quote. Each time I called, I was fobbed off with the same excuse that they were “waiting on a supplier for pricing”. This simply didn’t add up — they had already identified the parts, and I was able to find and price them myself from the very supplier they mentioned.

The quote eventually came through 8 days later. I accepted it immediately, only to then be told it would be at least another two weeks before they could carry out the repair.

I think it’s a joke that a company can charge a £120 call-out fee, give the impression they can resolve the issue quickly, and then expect you to wait a further 2–3 weeks without heating or hot water.

At this point, we had already been without heating and hot water for a prolonged period, with two young children at home, so this level of delay and lack of urgency was unacceptable.

I then contacted another company, who ordered the parts on next-day delivery and completed the repair the following day — which just shows how unnecessary the delays had been.

Overall, I felt completely misled and repeatedly fobbed off. The initial confidence quickly turned into poor communication, excuses, and unacceptable delays. I would not recommend this company.

I would strongly caution anyone booking through this company. If something goes wrong, you will bear the cost. My experience aligns with many other negative reviews, and it is clear that customers often end up paying the price.

UPDATE FOLLOWING DESTINATION 2 RESPONSE

As you can see by their response, Destination 2 appear to rely on their terms and conditions in a way that benefits them when unforeseen situations occur.

What is particularly frustrating is that they have not addressed our original request to change the hotel instead of cancelling it. Edit after reply:
This review has been written at the request of my mother in law who we accompanied to buy her motorhome.

On a side note after a little research it appears the newest 5* review has been flagged on a number of motorhome forums as being fake due to the fact he is family of the manager of Lancaster motorhomes and caravans and so the suspicious activity has been reported by numerous people.

My experience with Lancaster Motorhomes was deeply disappointing from start to finish. The sales process felt polished, but everything changed once payment was made. After-sales support was slow, unhelpful, and at times dismissive when issues were raised. The vehicle itself appeared poorly prepared, with faults that should have been identified before handover. There are also wider concerns on many forums about the authenticity of some recent Trustpilot and google 5* reviews (although it appears Trust pilot have now deleted a high number of reviews from the owners of the business) which didn’t match my experience at all. Overall, I would strongly advise others to do thorough research before committing.

My previous 1 star review was removed after I pointed out a series of suspicious 5 star reviews on Trustpilot- these have now been removed, suggesting my suspicions were correct.

Review now updated......

Initial sales process seemed very positive, but from the point of picking up the van, much more disappointing. Alarm bells rang when the low fuel alert came on before I'd got even got out of Carnforth- I don't expect a full tank, but enough fuel to make the 50 mile journey home would've been welcome.

Within the first couple of weeks of ownership, I discovered the leisure battery needed replacing and the vehicle battery was incompatible with the VW stop/start function. The service team agreed to rectify these issues, but it's concerning that neither were picked up as part of the pre-sales checks.

I later discovered that the vehicle had previously had an engine remap which had not been declared on the ad or mentioned during the sales process. I raised this with a Director who claimed this was not an issue and was unwilling to accept any responsibility for issues arising as a result of the mis-selling of the vehicle.

As a result of the above, my insurance company (NFU) requested an independent engineer report on the remap costing £210 and subsequently increased by premium by £350. The RAC warranty provided with the vehicle at a cost of £422 has also been invalidated as a result of the undeclared modification.

In short, in addition to initial problems which should have been resolved prior to sale, I am almost £1000 out of pocket as a result of the lack of transparency in the sales process and the refusal to take any responsibility for this.

Reading other reviews on Google, Trustpilot, Autotrader and motorhome forums, my experience is not unusual- LMC would rather try to portray unsatisfied customers as being unreasonable than have constructive conversations to resolve matters. In my case, the phone call I was promised by a Director never materialised and I was ultimately brushed off by email.

Understandably I would not recommend this company.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our 5year old Maine Coon, Loki, had two dental extraction surgeries at this practice within a year. Five weeks after his second surgery, he passed away from complications of acute renal decline.
Both times, Loki was prescribed an overdose of Metacam. Unknown to us at the time.

Prior to the first surgery, Loki's blood results were normal. When he returned to the practice ten months later, his bloods were no longer normal, and he was already in crisis. Despite this, we were told his results were normal, and we continued treatment for an oral issue under the uninformed belief that he was well.
He was not well

Loki declined rapidly after his second dental surgery. Blood tests six days later showed acute renal decline - His clinical picture was later confirmed by an independent expert as an IRIS graded acute kidney injury.
During this period, he also gained 2.4kg in just four weeks. Our concerns were repeatedly dismissed regarding this, until we took him for a second opinion.

It took over a year to obtain Loki’s full history. When I received it, I discovered Loki had been given the maximum guideline dose of injectable Metacam during both dental surgeries.
The manufacturer states, regarding this maximum dose:
“Repeated use of meloxicam in cats has been associated with acute renal failure and death. Do not administer additional meloxicam to cats”
Loki was prescribed additional Metacam (meloxicam) - he was always sent home with oral.

We were never made aware Loki had received injectable Metacam, and our informed consent for its use was never given. We believed we were the only ones providing pain relief. But the oral prescription after the injectable dose, was an overdose, as per manufacturer guidelines.

Despite Loki’s results indicating renal impairment, he was then put through further testing, including x-rays and a heart scan. What was needed was a stress free and inexpensive urine test to check his kidney function. We were only made aware of this after the heart scan.
Loki was referred and diagnosed with acute renal disease, but he was unable to recover.
The referral centre also received an incomplete medical history, leading to confusion around his acute decline and presentation.

I complained to IVC Evidensia, the practice owners, regarding Lokis 'care'.
In writing, they accepted that
‘Owners should be informed about abnormal findings’
'The practice should have used the licensed dose of Metacam or obtained informed consent for off-label use'.
IVC attempted to justify the overdosing by providing links to other manufacturers of meloxicam, stating they allow for higher dosing - this was verifiable false information.
They also stated it was 'not unreasonable' to give a higher dose, followed by 'guidelines can be confusing' and that they would use this 'opportunity' to review protocols and provide training to staff regarding rigorous use of this drug'

If the dosing was reasonable, why retrain staff? In my opinion, calling the death of a much loved family member an opportunity is highly insensitive. The guidelines are not confusing.
IVC repeatedly blamed hindsight, finally stating that the practice had acted in Loki’s best interests. I disagree.

According to Loki’s clinical history, three weeks before the second dental surgery, the same vet used the correct guideline dose for minor soft-tissue surgery, the dose that allows post-op oral Metacam. In my opinion, this was variable dosing depending on post-op pain levels, not confusion.

The dental surgeries mentioned were Loki’s second and third; his first was eight months earlier. After four requests for that record, made only after I questioned overdosing, it was provided. His medication history for that surgery is blank.

Four months after Loki died, on what would have been his sixth birthday, the practice called to remind us he was overdue his vaccinations.
I deeply regret trusting this practice with his wellbeing.
He was my favourite soul, and I miss him every day.

If other pet(cat) owners have had dental surgery here, before 2025, seriously consider a check up.

I have been a client of Greenlane Vets for over 20 years, but my recent experience which resulted in the loss of my 5‑year‑old Maine Coon cat Loki has been devastating and unacceptable.

Loki had pre‑operative bloods taken on 4th June 2024 before a routine dental. Those results were not compatible with proceeding safely, yet this was never communicated to us. Despite having blood results that were “off the scale”, the practice went ahead with the dental surgery. To which he never recovered from, after multiple visits he had to endure a second procedure where Loki was given an excessive dose of Metacam. IVC (owners of Greenlane) later acknowledged that Greenlane had administered this excessive dose without consent, they even described the excessive Metacam dose as “reasonable”, yet in the same correspondence stated that drug guidelines can be “confusing” and that they would “take this opportunity to retrain staff”  an admission that directly contradicts their claim that the overdose was acceptable.

Over the following weeks, Loki became increasingly unwell. His condition deteriorated rapidly after the second surgery, during where he received the excessive dose of Metacam, and he then began gaining weight. At the time, we were told he was “eating too much”. Only later did we learn that these changes were consistent with an acute renal decline something already visible in his blood results but never communicated to us.

When an out‑of‑hours vet advised that Greenlane were out of their depth and recommended referral, Greenlane insisted that Loki undergo £1,700 worth of what they described as “gold standard” tests before they would agree to refer him. These tests included repeat bloods which showed that Loki had an acute kidney injury compared to his previous results again, something they failed to communicate to us. Despite this, they claimed he had a heart issue and recommended a heart scan the next day, even though the bloods directly disputed this. They still insisted on the heart scan before proceeding with the referral. Even after insisting on these tests, they failed to pass on key clinical information to the referral centre.

From Loki’s first presentation for a routine procedure to his death was just eight weeks. He was five years old and the most kind natured cat you would never meet. The responses from both Greenlane and IVC have been dismissive, defensive, and centred on blaming hindsight rather than accepting responsibility. Both the practice and IVC have repeatedly weaponised hindsight to minimise their failings, despite being in possession of the clinical findings first‑hand and failing to act on them at every stage.

After Loki’s death, it also came to light six months later, and only after persistently requesting his full clinical history that he had been given yet another excessive dose of Metacam on another surgery and this had never been disclosed to us at the time. One of the vets involved in these failures is no longer with the practice, but another remains including the vet who contributed to the excessive dose Loki received. The fact that multiple overdoses only emerged months after his death raises serious concerns about how many other cats may have been put at risk during dental procedures up until 2025 given that these incidents were not recorded transparently or communicated to owners.

After two decades as a loyal client, I can no longer trust this practice with the care of any animal, we hope the RCVS recognise this as misconduct. We feel that we failed Loki by taking him to Greenlane and we miss him dearly.

After refreshing emails for 3 hours and even having a senior agent pretend his phone wasn't working while I was mid-sentence, it came to light that the tenant property manager Ben was blocking the application due to a personal "blanket pet ban."

It is highly unprofessional for an agent to interfere when both the landlord and block management have given permission. Working in real estate myself, I know that these "politics" result in properties sitting vacant longer than necessary because an agent’s bias trumps a landlord’s preference. They allowed me to view the property and wait for hours for an email they NEVER intended to send. Extremely dishonest.

Note to the agency: I anticipate a reply citing "technical issues" or "missing emails," or a new version of events, but let’s be clear: the failure to send the form prior to the viewing—as your own staff confirmed should have happened— and for the 1hr 30mins after the viewing when I called several times - was a deliberate block. I am quite disappointed with the service I received from Ben’s Gutters.

When booking the appointment, I was informed that it would take between 30 - 60 minutes, and would feature my gutters being washed through (internally) and would cost £87. However:

1) The guy turned up at my front door 20 minutes earlier than the earliest agreed time. (Check their reviews - a lot of people have the same complaint).

2) The appointment took 17 minutes only - not 30 to 60 minutes. He arrived at 09:08, and left at 09:25. I have verified this on my CCTV. (Check their reviews - me, Tim, Matthew, Jemma, Phoebe, Paul, Dominic, Angel, Edward, Sam, Danita, Zara, Claudia, Ioanna, Steven, Andrew and Rachel have all made the same complaint.)

3) He climbed a ladder, lifted some leaves out of the gutter, put them into a bucket and left. That’s all. I’d assumed that they had some special cleaning equipment - but no. Literally just a guy and a bucket.

4) I was told that he would wash the gutters through with water. This didn’t happen. The photos of the job (which I had to contact Ben’s Gutters to obtain) show dirty gutters.

5) I was told that he should disassemble the downpipes to check/clean them. This also didn’t happen. How did they know that they weren’t blocked unless they checked?

I contacted Ben’s Gutters, who offered to reduce the bill to £60. Given the early arrival, quick finish, lack of cleaning, lack of taking the gutters apart, and the fact that it was literally a guy with a bucket, I felt that this wasn’t a suitable discount.

I have emailed Ben’s Gutters about this, citing specific elements of GDPR, and have been told that they will ‘update’ me. As of yet, I have not received this update. I will update this review when I have.

So - all in all - it would have been cheaper, better and more legal for me to offer someone in a local Facebook group £40 or so to lift the leaves out of the gutter into a bucket. I’ll likely do that next time. Ben’s Gutter's, for the service they supply, is over priced, over sold and poor quality.

I WAS very impressed with my Nilfisk P200 Pressure Washer. Top of the range. Cleans well.
(Edit since post - I have a workaround - not ideal but it works for me. Put a smear of fairy liquid or similar on the male bayonets and they slide in fairly easily. Long terms this probably eats the o-rings but I found sets of o-rings in hardware stores that fit and work perfectly and much cheaper than the Nilfisk “spares”).

Original post :
Having bought it in July 2024, I’ve used it for a total of about 8 hours over 4 months.
Carefully followed the instructions about lubricating the various bayonet joints.
Winterised the unit from Nov to March.
Came to use it and the bayonets will not mate.
Asked Nilfisk customer service who eventually told me “it’s the O-rings - they go hard, you need to follow the link and buy a spare set”.
£18.99.
The entire unit is currently unusable as the spray heads will not attach. And if they do I worry they won’t detach as they are very tight.

Now bearing in mind I have 2 spray heads, an extension lance and a patio head, I need 4 o-rings.  The spare pack has only 2 of that size, so need to buy 2 sets totalling £38.
As the first set has “hardened” after 4 months, I might need to replace them again before end of 2025.  So potentially £76 in seals per year.
I realise seals are “consumables” and not covered by warranty but strikes me as a planned ransom - by fitting poor quality seals that harden within weeks - to keep this prime quality piece of kit working.
Asked Nilfisk to send a set of seals free of charge as a gesture of goodwill. No resposne.
Not impressed. Not happy.
Would not buy another.
My old £180 Spear & Jackson unit may not have the same pressure or flowrate as the Nilfisk P200 but it’s been running for 5 years with bi-weekly use cleaning cars and never needed a spare part or repair.

We also noticed quite a lot of damage to the vehicle, despite being told it had “only been out a few times.” There was damage to the table base, to the lid of the hob and the base boards were all scuffed and scraped.

While loading our things, I picked up what I thought was a cleaning rag from inside the bedside wardrobe, but it turned out to be dirty knickers left behind from a previous hire. Once we set off, we did enjoy ourselves. We loved having a bacon butty in the car park at Gretna Green and stopping in the middle of the hills for a cup of tea and a biscuit. However, the tyre pressure alarms went off as soon as we left the yard, and the onboard system kept giving conflicting messages about the water and waste tanks — one minute full, the next empty.

Returning the motorhome was just as chaotic. Again, no one was at the yard. After about 10 minutes the cleaner arrived, but she had no idea how to take delivery of the vehicle. She phoned one of the owners, who told her just to take the keys and they’d check it later. I asked for the phone and spoke to the other owner, this time a lady, and mentioned the dirty knickers, and she again blamed a “new cleaner.” I also mentioned that a driver had stopped us to say the brake lights weren’t working — something we were never told.

We then waited 19 days for our deposit to be returned, only receiving it after chasing twice. For a small business, customer service should be a priority, but sadly it felt severely lacking throughout. I don’t want to hear excuses about new cleaners — train your staff properly from the start and the blame game is just an excuse for arrogance.

one_star_reviews.text:
3 months into our tenancy we've experienced the following with Bridgfords (Burnley branch)/Countrywide (Preston branch)/Entwistle Green (no, I've no idea why they all take turns to email me or why they have different names if they're basically all the same company):

*Being given details of a property manager no longer in their employ on our move-in day. Trying to contact them had an email reply of "they no longer work for us" then someone from Entwistle Green replied later on instead. A Bridgfords employee later told me "they left a month ago". okay cool, so why was I given their contact details on a printed sheet of paper?

*Being told I'd incorrectly logged repair reports online & on the wrong site, despite following the printed handout we were given upon arrival to the letter. when I explained, all I was met with was "what's the name of the person who gave you this information". I didn't really care about that, I just wanted the repairs done. This employee then ghosted us and never messaged back.

*several issues we reported in our first week STILL have not been addressed, it's a joke.

*Took around a month of emails/calls with various Bridgfords employees just to get somebody to sort our broken boiler and thermostat out; we had no heating all that time.

*we were instructed to order a bin from the local council & pay for the bin ourselves, then minus that fee from our next rent payment. despite being told to do this, Countrywide/Bridgfords sent us a threatening email saying we were in rent arrears. I replied back saying this was rubbish, only to be ignored for two days. I only got a reply when I sent a follow up saying I would message literally every day until they backed off and apologised. Funnily enough, 5 mins later, they finally replied.

*for some reason took a month for them to remove the 'for rent' sign outside. again, soon as I complained, it magically disappeared shortly after.

*I had to fix a broken kitchen drawer myself within the first month because they refused to acknowledge the issue which was present since day 1.

*Their customer service is woefully slow. if you want to communicate via email, you get whinged at and pushed towards phone calls, which you then get dumped onto hold for and have patchy reception anyway.

*we've had 3, soon to be 4, visits from a contractor with regards to our bath/shower. how it takes this many call outs to repair one tap is beyond me. but apparently i'm 'unreasonable' to expect a different contractor to have a go at the repairs. hmm, okay. THAT seems unreasonable itself.

*the latest instance of the contractor coming around has now broken the bath tap, no hot water, the seal is leaking, he's caused some damage to the kitchen & even our front door seems damaged due to some equipment he'd had resting against the door for an hour.

What does Bridgfords/Countrywide have to say about this? "You should have pointed it out at the time to avoid another unnecessary visit to the property".

Yeah okay, i'm so sorry for being a dumb tenant who didn't refuse to let a contractor leave until i'd magically detected various issues around the house and bullied him into fixing them. if we'd arranged for this repair to take place when we were out of the house anyway, what would this Countrywide employee of yours have said to me then, "you should have stayed at home and not gone to work to prevent another home visit". what nonsense. this woman is on another planet. I've filed a formal report against her because she shouldn't be offering her own opinions. for a supposed professional, her entire email was nasty and sneering.

What's odd is normally this Bridgfords branch itself that would reply to repair concerns; it just reeks of being fobbed off to another team, as if they're sick of my emails after all these months. If things got sorted & without the patronising comments, or being ignored, we wouldn't have this trouble.

all in all, incredibly useless company.
BUT I will be happy to update my review with positives if they actually prove they can deliver from now on. We shall see...

"4 Years of Hell, & ongoing". How long does it take to fit a kitchen properly? - still waiting.
I paid Wickes in 2021 for them to fit my kitchen & utility room, & I'm still waiting for it to be finished, by a 3rd Wickes approved installer.
On 30th September 2024 the 1st installation was eventually (after 2 year & 6 months) ripped out & refitted again for a second time by Wickes installers. Endorsed by the Ombudsman due to how badly it had been fitted 1st time round in March 2022 in only 9 days. It had to be completely re plastered, re tiled & re fitted with new cupboards, & the previous appliances fitted back. This time it was fitted over 3 weeks to give a week for the plaster to dry (instead of less than 24 hours as previous, before fitting wooden cupboards).
Now Wickes has had 2 attempts to install my kitchen & utility room, I feel so very very let down. -The floor and wall tiling has not been done to trading standards (again), disappointed that my utility room sink has not been fitted back in the same place as previous, electric socket not fitted back properly, wall and floor cupboards carcasses & surrounds not level & gaps along inside edge & areas not sealed down properly, skirting board cut into with radiator pipes not secure to wall properly, door frame ripped off before plastering & re fitted back cracked, cheap thin plastic main water supply pipework (installed instead of the original copper) with stop tap too small, plus more issues.
We paid over 20 thousand for this, & it is still not right. It's gone 4 years now from 1st bodge installation, & 1 year 6 months from 2nd bodge installation, overall I've sent Wickes hundreds of emails, plus hundreds of photos & videos from compaints about 1st installation &  complaints about 2nd installation, & have always felt fobbed off when eventually they email back. - Still waiting to know what they intend to do to sort out all the issues from this 2nd installation.
Wickes say they struggled for months to locate another installer saying- 'unfortunately this is proving more difficult than usual as there is a shortage of installers in the area & they are having to look further afield '. However they did find 1 that they have used before, that doesn't live far away at all. They sent around a 3rd installer 4 months ago for site visit to see what needs doing, who seems very nice and keen to do a good job, who could have done it by now - March 2026. But Wickes were not happy him saying our kitchen & utility room needs a full re fit. So Wickes told the installer he had to come back again.- And he did last month, to do a list of materials needed for what Wickes is prepared to do.
Wickes has still not shared with us a list of work that They propose to do, & when, (despite my repeat emails to them). So we Still Have No Date as to when or what year our kitchen & utility room will be finished.
This kitchen installation (my husband & I picked in 2021) was meant to have made me happy, after undergoing many years of cancer treatment. But It's been immensely stressful for over 4 years so far. The excessively long waiting times to receive emails back, & huge delays (of years) Wickes are deliberately taking to try not to resolve issues is disgusting.
My advice to others is, (although the staff seem nice in the shop,) avoid this company for kitchen installations, as the service is not fit for purpose. And Customer Relations is just there to fob the customer off until they give up.

OK Diner? Not OK

Really disappointed with our visit to OK Diner. The service was terrible from start to finish.

Lots of menu items weren’t available and nobody told us beforehand — including no hot dogs and no Coca-Cola. We only found out after trying to order them.

We were a party of 6, and after a very long wait they brought out just two meals without saying a word, then disappeared for another 20 minutes while the rest of us sat there waiting. There was only around 5 other tables so it definitely wasn’t busy. Other tables that arrived after us were getting their food while we had to keep chasing staff to find out what was happening. By the time the rest of the food finally arrived, the first two meals had gone cold.

My partner politely went to the bar to ask where the rest of the food was and pointed out that they could have at least explained there was a delay when they brought the first plates out. Instead of apologising, four members of staff started arguing with him.

When the food finally came, it was alright at best. The fries were lukewarm and the burger was nowhere near worth £15 — we could have made a much better one at home.

The cleanliness of the restaurant was also appalling. The tables and chairs were sticky, and both the male and female toilets were out of use, meaning everyone had to use the disabled toilet. I think Kim and Aggie need to pay a visit because I don’t think that toilet has ever seen bleach or a mop.

Overall, awful service, poor communication, long waits, disappointing food, and poor hygiene standards. Sadly, we won’t be back.

It is with a profound sense of civic alarm and professional distaste that I record my impressions of a recent encounter with a representative of your firm, a technician named "Danny Birkett." While one expects a specialist in vermin disposal to maintain a focus on the mechanical and biological realities of the task, I was instead subjected to a verbal odyssey of the most jarring and prejudiced nature.
Upon my inquiry regarding the ethical and procedural nuances of his work, Mr. Birkett did not offer a technical explanation. Instead, he utilized the opportunity to launch into a protracted and vitriolic monologue concerning the most vulnerable echelons of our society. He spoke with a disturbing lack of empathy about those battling addiction, individuals navigating the complexities of the care system, and those who have endured profound struggle in their personal lives. It was an unprovoked display of hostility toward his fellow man, delivered with the weary condescension of one who believes their own narrow perspective to be an objective truth.
One expects a certain baseline of professional distance and human decency in a service encounter, yet Danny Birkett’s conduct suggests a profound ontological mismatch with any role requiring public interaction. His interpersonal frequency is tuned exclusively to a channel of judgment and derision. To hear a professional representative speak so disparagingly of those facing systemic and personal hardship was nothing short of a masterclass in modern callousness.
Furthermore, having navigated the interpersonal wreckage of other local service providers, I was at least relieved to find that no one named "Jackie" was involved in this particular debacle. It is a small, hollow mercy to know that "PTSD" from her specific brand of passive aggression was not a factor here, though Mr. Birkett’s own verbal vitriol was a more than capable substitute.
In conclusion, I must express my sincere hope that Mr. Birkett’s tenure with your organization is swiftly and decisively terminated, much like the very vermin he is tasked to dispose of. Such a corrosive temperament has no place in a professional setting. I shall look forward to the day I encounter him in a more suitable environment, perhaps at the local "Sainsbury’s," where he might find honest labor stocking shelves, a vocation that mercifully requires no intellectual engagement with the public and offers no platform for his particular brand of social malice. Until that time, I shall be seeking my pest control solutions elsewhere.

⭐ 1 Star – Avoid at all costs

Our problems with Livingway at Edward House started almost immediately after moving in, and the experience only got worse over time.

The heating/AC unit was faulty from the beginning, constantly cutting off. We contacted Livingway for months and were repeatedly told the job had been “put out,” but nothing was ever actually done. By the time summer came, the flat became unbearable — temperatures inside went over 35°C. I even called the emergency line, only to be told it “wasn’t an emergency” and to call back another day. The issue wasn’t resolved until January 2026, nearly a full year after we moved in.

Things escalated further when I came home from a 12-hour shift to find a leak in the flat. When the emergency team attended, they showed me that there had been no hose connected to the back of the unit, meaning it had likely been leaking for months.This could have caused damp and mould in both the living room and bedroom.

When maintenance came out, they initially denied the mould, then simply painted over it with mould paint. As shown in the photos, the mould was still clearly visible. To make matters worse, paint was left all over the carpet inside our flat and even on the carpet outside in the communal area, showing a complete lack of care and professionalism. I took it upon myself to clean this up before we got charged for this during the move out based on other reviews.

The condition of the building itself was also unacceptable — the bin area was absolutely disgusting, constantly overflowing and clearly not maintained properly.

There was also misleading information in the adverts. The listing on Rightmove stated that WiFi was included, which is completely untrue. Even after we gave notice, they have continued advertising the property with WiFi included, despite this not being the case.

We also experienced issues with the rent system being changed, which led to confusion and a backlog of rent through no fault of our own. This added unnecessary stress on top of an already poor experience.

Communication was extremely poor. I specifically asked Livingway to contact my partner during the day, as I work in healthcare and cannot take calls while caring for seriously ill patients. Despite this, they repeatedly called me anyway. Even after explaining my situation, the calls continued.

Other issues included:
•Washing machine breaking and flooding the living room doorway, ruining our towels
•Living room window that wouldn’t lock (reported at 6-month inspection and still not fixed by move-out)
•Wardrobe broken within the first week and left unrepaired for months
•No blinds in any room for almost 3 weeks after we moved in
•Bathroom sink wouldn’t drain without you lifting it

Overall, this has been a stressful and exhausting experience. Basic maintenance, safety issues, and tenant concerns were consistently ignored or poorly handled. I would not recommend renting with Livingway based on our experience.

I have visited the South Tynedale Railway many times over the years, and it’s a railway I feel has a lot of potential, which is why some recent developments have been disappointing.

While the extension to Slaggyford runs through attractive countryside, the reality is that there is very little to do at the current terminus. Aside from the buffet coach at the station there are no shops, pubs, or cafés in the village, which can make the wait for the return train unnecessarily long if you are not planning to go walking.

As an enthusiast, I was also extremely disappointed by the recent work carried out on historic steam locomotive "Barber". In my opinion the locomotive’s distinctive historic appearance has been unnecessarily altered, creating a rather odd and unattractive looking engine. It also appears that original material may have been altered or lost in the process. The reasoning given for these changes has been widely questioned, and the work could instead have been carried out in a way that preserved more of the locomotive’s original character, for example by following the appearance of its sister engine "Masham". The way this was handled has been very controversial and has clearly divided opinion within the enthusiast community.

It is also disappointing to see the railway using AI-generated images in its advertising. For a heritage railway, it would be far more appropriate to use genuine photography of the line or support real artists.

Overall, this railway still has potential given its scenic location, but recent decisions have made it difficult to feel enthusiastic about visiting again.

I had an extremely disappointing experience with this firm while in the process of purchasing a property. We were just two weeks away from exchange, and throughout that time they continued to respond to enquiries and engage with our solicitor as if the transaction was progressing as normal.

However, without any warning or communication, they proceeded to exchange and complete with another buyer. At no point did they indicate that this was a possibility or that our position was at risk. This lack of transparency is completely unacceptable, especially given how close we were to exchange and the level of commitment already involved.

Their actions not only wasted a significant amount of time and money but also caused considerable stress and frustration. Professional standards in conveyancing should include clear and honest communication, which was entirely lacking here.

I would strongly advise others to be cautious when dealing with this firm.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐☆☆☆☆

I have had an extremely disappointing experience with Castle Green Homes since moving into my property nearly three years ago. The level of after-sales care and customer service has been unacceptable throughout.

Many of my snagging issues took over 12 months to be addressed, while jobs were repeatedly closed on the Willow portal without explanation or completion. Calls and emails often went unanswered for months. Shortly after moving in, I was left without heating and hot water for five days and had to shower at work.

I was promised my back garden would be turfed, yet after 18 months of chasing I was eventually told Castle Green no longer intended to honour the agreement. Only after providing proof and escalating the matter did contractors finally attend — and they simply laid turf directly over weeds without properly preparing the ground. During this visit, inappropriate comments were also made about my garden being a “dump”, despite the condition being caused by Castle Green’s delays.

When the garden was eventually re-turfed months later, the turf was already infected with clover weed which quickly spread. Despite reporting this immediately, nothing has been done.

I have also dealt with a leaking bath that caused damage to my living room ceiling, which took over four months to repair despite repeated reports. My bathroom extractor fan has failed around six times, with repairs often taking four months each time, leaving my bathroom covered in mould for much of the time I’ve lived here. On one occasion, a director accused me of making the issue up before eventually attending and confirming the fan had failed again. It has since failed once more.

Attempts to raise a formal complaint were repeatedly blocked, with calls even being terminated when I requested to escalate matters.

The overall experience has been stressful, exhausting, and completely unacceptable for a new-build property. I have now involved NHBC and am seeking legal advice due to the ongoing issues and health concerns caused by persistent mould and unresolved defects.

I am still without a working extractor fan, still no garden, and there are still outstanding decorative works to be done over three years into living at the property. I have sent 2 emails since my last response from Castle Green in April with no response nor acknowledgment.

I would strongly advise anyone considering purchasing from Castle Green Homes to think very carefully before doing so.

We moved into our home with Castle Green Home almost three years ago, trusting that we were buying a well-built, properly managed property. Unfortunately, our experience since then has been incredibly disappointing.

From early on, any issues we raised were largely ignored or dismissed, with little to no follow-up. Communication has consistently been poor, leaving us feeling completely unsupported as homeowners.

The situation became far worse last summer, when the entire estate was informed that the water pipes installed under our homes did not meet Welsh Water regulations. This resulted in every property having their gardens and driveways dug up. What made this even more frustrating was being told initially that the work would take “around a month.”

In reality, many of us have effectively been displaced for nearly a year, living on a business site while the work dragged on. Throughout this time, communication from Castle Green has been minimal at best. Updates have been vague, infrequent, or non-existent, leaving residents constantly chasing for information and clarity.

This has caused significant disruption to daily life, stress, and a complete loss of trust in a company we once had confidence in. For a developer of this size, the lack of accountability, planning, and basic communication is unacceptable.

I would strongly advise anyone considering buying from Castle Green Home to think carefully and ensure they are prepared for the possibility of poor aftercare and communication if things go wrong
